correctness.rationale: Reconstructed normalization from classical Thue–Morse autocorrelation recurrences. The base values at n=4,5,6,7 give integral rescaled adjacent pairs with odd coordinate sum; two exact integer matrices preserve this invariant, and for all child odd frequencies the first coordinate is odd. Every positive frequency reduces by powers of two to an odd one, proving exactly the two zero orbits and the valuation; Fourier diagonalization proves the nullspace. Exact Fraction and independent integer-matrix computations agree for 65,535 indices. Limits: checker is finite, full proof is analytic and assumes the classical existence of autocorrelations.

originality.rationale: The reviewed classical Thue–Morse papers provide the recurrence, spectral measure and some infinite zero families, but do not state the exact two-orbit zero set, the exact odd-frequency dyadic valuation, or the Fourier-convolution annihilator. The new integral parity invariant rules out all other zeros at once. A 1990 source about autocorrelations could not be read in full, so the assessment remains bounded and not a mathematical proof of novelty.
residual_risks: The 1990 IEEE synchronization paper may have a stronger hidden autocorrelation statement; complete text was not accessible, so originality remains bounded.
Other older automatic-sequence or mathematical-diffraction literature may contain the same parity induction under different terminology; no proof of worldwide uniqueness is claimed.
Finite exact checks do not independently validate every infinite index; the recurrence induction is the proof.

value.rationale: The complete zero set is a natural invariant of the canonical singular continuous Thue–Morse diffraction measure and specifies exactly which Fourier modes its convolution operator annihilates, at all scales. The integer-matrix parity law also gives precise rational 2-adic valuations for every large odd frequency and an exact logarithmic zero-count law in dyadic spectral windows; those are not merely a small computation or renaming of a known example. The 2008/2022 recurrence and the 2025 partial zero orbit motivate the mathematical gap. Limit: nonzero magnitudes and exact spectral distribution are not determined.
